maya: Heads up — after the 4-bit quant bring-up, pass@k dropped but BERTScore went up on the QA eval set. Not sure why, looks contradictory.
kevin: Can you paste the exact eval_runner command, seed, and quant args?
maya: ```
./eval_runner 
  --model /models/qa/bertq-4bit/commit-abc123 
  --task squad_like 
  --seed 42 
  --samples 200 
  --k 5 
  --batch-size 8 
  --quant config=qlora,mode=4bit
```
sam: CI shows the job green earlier, but local runs are noisier. Any logs/artifacts?
maya: partial metric dump from my run: 
```
{"pass_at_k": 0.18, "bertscore_f1": 0.862, "exact_match": 0.71, "ece": 0.18}
```
toni: I also spotted that our calibration histogram is very clustered near 0.95+. Are we accidentally using sigmoid per-candidate anywhere?
maya: Good catch — I grepped the metric impl: eval/metrics/prob_calib.py has a snippet doing sigmoid(logits) per candidate then normalizing. That seems wrong for multi-candidate selection.
kevin: That is wrong. pass@k math assumes multinomial sampling over softmax-normalized logits or sampling-without-replacement based on softmax weights. Applying sigmoid independently and normalizing changes relative odds significantly.
maya: Also the sampler is doing sampling-with-replacement then deduping ids later, which reduces effective k. Log message I saw: 
```
WARNING: sampler produced duplicate ids, effective_k=3
```
sam: That explains a lower pass@k (fewer unique candidates). BERTScore could increase if the quantized model produces more conservative / high-prob repeated n-best items — less diversity but higher semantic match.
kevin: Two things to fix: (A) change calibration -> softmax over logits (with stable logit clamp), compute probabilities, then compute ECE/Brier; (B) sampler: explicit without-replacement sampling or sample until unique K collected (but deterministic). Also clamp logits to avoid overflow before softmax (e.g., x - max(x)).
maya: I prototyped fixes and added unit tests with synthetic logits. Also added brier_score and ECE to the eval output. Opening PR: https://git.redwood.internal/p/R/redwood-eval/+/4298
ci-bot: CI report: eval-runner job #2734 failed 2/3 on timeout (15m). When it times out it stops before metrics flush.
sam: CI flakiness likely from batch-size=8 with KV-cache thrash on small instances. For CI smoke we should force batch-size=1 or run smaller sample count.
toni: Also double-check tokenizer: a change in tokenization (truncation/space handling) can move BERTScore. Are tokenizers pinned?
maya: Tokenizer is pinned to v0.9 in model repo. I compared tokens; outputs are slightly shorter after quant due to beam pruning differences. That explains higher BERTScore (shorter but focused answers).
kevin: Good. After PR we should: add deterministic RNG seed test, add a small randomized integration test that asserts pass@k computation matches a reference implementation (numpy-based), and add a CI smoke that runs quant path.
maya: Local after fixes (PR branch): ``pass@5=0.24, bscore_f1=0.850, exact_match=0.72, ece=0.07`` Baseline master: ``pass@5=0.25, bscore_f1=0.845, exact_match=0.73, ece=0.05`` — pretty close.
sam: That's acceptable for canary. Add an eval-dashboard note to track pass@k drift vs baseline for next 24h.
kevin: :thumbsup: We should also add a small note in model-onboarding checklist: "ensure sampler without-replacement for ranked n-best" and "verify calibration uses softmax for multinomial tasks".
maya: Done in PR description. Also added a small reproducibility notebook under eval/tools/repro.ipynb that shows both implementations side-by-side.
kevin: Great. Once CI passes on PR 4298, let's run a canary rollout on dedicated infra with 1% traffic.
eval-bot: Deploy canary created: canary/quant-4bit/2025-11-03 id=cny-991. Monitoring dashboards linked.
ci-bot: CI passed on PR 4298 (flaky retried once). Artifacts: /artifacts/eval/4298/report.html
maya: Thanks all. Follow-ups: add softmax-clamp utility to runtime, add E2E test for duplicate sampling case, add better logging (effective_k).
toni: Also file an infra ticket to increase timeout for long evals or split into chunks.
kevin: I'll follow up on infra ticket.
maya: closing the loop — metrics look sane now, merging later today unless objections. :party:
